source.excerpt: Rest satisfied with doing well, and leave others to talk of you as they please.
trail: Wikiquote and LibQuotes both point to The World’s Laconics (1853). That is a citation to a later collection, not evidence of Pythagoras’s exact words. This research did not inspect the collection’s page or find an ancient passage behind this rendering. Attribution and book lead ↗
LibQuotes repeats the wording and names the same 1853 book without an ancient locator. Matching collection citation ↗

author.heading: About Pythagoras
author.bio: Pythagoras became the subject of a large later tradition of ethical sayings. Establishing the source of one English maxim requires more than matching it to that familiar reputation.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: The inspected references lead to a nineteenth-century collection rather than a located ancient passage. Its advice about private satisfaction and public criticism may suit an ethical anthology, but that suitability is not evidence that Pythagoras originated the exact words.
